svg.title: Two ways molecules cross a membrane
svg.desc: (a) A semipermeable membrane drawn as a column of blocks separated by narrow gaps, the pores. Molecules of many sizes lie on both sides. Only the smallest fit through the pores: one small molecule passes right and another passes left, while the large molecules stay where they are. (b) Molecules packed closely on both sides of a solid membrane. A few of them have dissolved in the membrane and are diffusing across it. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A semipermeable membrane sorts by size
Schematic, not to scale. Molecules smaller than the pores cross in both directions; larger ones
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
